rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is read off declaration-lines-825.scala. Three mechanisms put a relationship on a line its name is not written on, all three found by the M59 oracle over real scala3 sources, all three the same defect: the line belongs to the NAME, not to the construct containing it. (1) A definition with a leading annotation: tree-sitter-scala starts the definition node AT the annotation, so `contains Annotated -> countdown` landed on `@tailrec` (24) instead of `def countdown` (25), and the symbol's own range was wrong the same way. (2) A multi-line inheritance list: `with Mixin` / `with Product` were both stamped with the line the `extends` clause opened on (32). (3) A multi-line type expression: `List` and `Option` were stamped with the line the enclosing type expression opened on (39) instead of their own (40, 41). At the 300-file scala scale these three accounted for every remaining oracle failure (8 of 8). The forbidRelationships entries are the pre-fix behaviour, so a regression fails the gate instead of passing silently.
